correctness.rationale: In a nonempty maximal independent set, clockwise gaps are 2 or 3; fixing one vertex roots an ordered composition, and fixing a second independently roots both arcs. Thus the one- and two-site incidence counts are b_n and b_d b_(n−d), including d=1 where the latter is zero. Perrin recurrence and lengths 3,4,5 give P_n=2b_n+b_(n−3). Expanding the two Walsh signs yields H(n,d)=4b_d b_(n−d)−2b_(n−2)−b_(n−3). The constant mode is positive, the singleton multiplier b_(n−3) vanishes only at n=4, and adjacency gives a strictly negative pair multiplier. The exact seeds at distances 2 through 9 suffice: each later H is the sum of its two- and three-step predecessors, and all earlier feasible lengths in those rows are accounted for. For larger distances use d≤n/2 and the proven bounds 0.408<b_k/λ^k<0.421 for all k≥10; they propagate from 10,11,12 because λ^(−2)+λ^(−3)=1. The strict rational comparison 4·0.408²>0.421(2/L²+1/L³) at L=1.324717957 enforces H>0 when both arcs are at least 10. Thus the finite check is not used to infer infinite nonvanishing. At n=9 each of distances 3 and 4 has nine unordered pairs; ordinary unnormalized convolution multiplies each Walsh character by its own coefficient.
residual_risks: The claim and the audit concern only degrees 0–2, simple labelled cycles n≥3, and the uniform indicator, not a greedy sampling law or full-spectrum invertibility.

value.rationale: The restricted low-degree band has a natural role: it comprises all linear and pair statistics of the vertex bits. Exact identification of which such signals are erased by this unweighted averaging is a useful discrimination even when the full operator is singular. The result is a complete invariant for this band at every cycle length, not a repetition of the known count formula or a cutoff picked after an enumeration.
residual_risks: No consequence for the rank on higher Walsh degrees or for other graph families is claimed.
